setting: You are all in Cornwall, England, and you know each other as siblings who grew up in the same family home in the county. You are now grown up and spread across nearby towns, keeping in touch through this group chat while you plan a birthday outing for your mum.

Rachel.knows: You are the eldest sibling, and Daniel and Lucy are your younger brother and sister, whom you have looked out for since childhood.
Rachel.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something needs sorting or when you have a spare moment between shifts.
Rachel.style: Little emoji and few texting abbreviations, mostly full words.

Daniel.knows: You are the middle sibling, sitting between Rachel's steady sense of responsibility and Lucy's easy warmth, and you have always been the one who fixes things for the family.
Daniel.texts: You message in this chat fairly often, usually to chip in with practical suggestions when plans come up.
Daniel.style: Some emoji and a few casual abbreviations.

Lucy.knows: You are the youngest sibling, and Rachel and Daniel are your older siblings, the one who keeps everyone laughing and the one you have always gone to for advice.
Lucy.texts: You message in this chat often, quick to reply and happy to start conversations about plans.
Lucy.style: Plenty of emoji and lots of texting abbreviations.

private_lines.Rachel: You work as a paramedic on shifts covering towns across Cornwall, so your days swing between early starts, late finishes and the odd night shift. You live alone in a small terraced house in Truro, and you usually unwind with a run or a quiet evening when you are off.
private_lines.Daniel: You work as a self-employed electrician, travelling to jobs around west Cornwall, so your days start early and depend on the weather and client bookings. You live in Penzance with your partner and a rescue dog, and you spend evenings at home or at the pub with mates.
private_lines.Lucy: You work as a veterinary nurse at a clinic in St Austell, with days that run from morning until early evening and the occasional weekend shift. You live in a flat in St Austell and spend your free time walking with friends or seeing your animal-loving circle.

situation: Siblings planning a birthday outing for their mum.
topic: What are the opening hours of the Eden Project in Cornwall in December?

@claude what are the opening hours of the Eden Project in Cornwall in December? And is it open every day that month?

I couldn't open Eden's opening-times page, so I can't confirm the standard December hours or whether it's open every day. Eden's Christmas listings suggest the Biomes close to day visitors at 15:15 on Christmas Lights days. They then reopen from 16:00 to 20:30 for the lights evenings. Those run on most December dates but not 24 or 25 December. Check https://edenproject.com/visit/opening-times before choosing a day.
